research_rationale: Executive Order 11963 of January 19, 1977 (42 FR 4325) has two sections, both amending Executive Order 10900 of January 5, 1961 (administration of the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954): section 1 adds a subsection (d) to section 1 of Executive Order 10900 directing the Secretary of Agriculture, after consultation with named officials, to transmit to the Congress the reports required by section 408 of the Act, and section 2 revokes section 5 of Executive Order 10900 and redesignates sections 6, 7 and 8 as 5, 6 and 7. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21-strike-and-insert.md an amendment continues, as part of the amended order, until the parent order ends. Executive Order 12220 of June 27, 1980 (45 FR 44245), section 1-501, revokes Executive Order 10900 as amended; it takes effect on signing and states no later date. That is the first end for both sections. The same reporting direction is reissued independently in Executive Order 12220, so the function continues under a different order. The reading that section 2, an instruction executed when issued, was exhausted on January 19, 1977 and only its consequence survived is the alternative a reviewer should see; it would not change the order-level end date of June 27, 1980, which is set by section 1. The 7 U.S.C. 1691 note in the U.S. Code release point 119-121 lists this order as an amending order of Executive Order 10900 and carries that order's ended status line.
savings_reason: Executive Order 12220, in its own section on the Department of Agriculture, directs the Secretary of Agriculture, after the same consultation, to transmit to the Congress all reports required by section 408 of the Act; that reissued command is independent of Executive Order 11963 and continues under Executive Order 12220 until that order's own end, which is outside this claim.
earlier_end_check: Later orders touching Executive Order 10900 were checked: Executive Order 12148 (1979-07-20) revokes only section 4(d)(2) (foreign currencies for the supplemental stockpile) and Executive Order 12163 (1979-09-29) amends section 3 by adding a subsection; neither touches the added section 1(d) or the revoked section 5, so no earlier end exists. Executive Order 10915 (1961-01-24) precedes this order; it inserted a new section 6 and renumbered sections 6 and 7, which is why this order redesignates sections 6, 7 and 8. The ofr_catalog search lists 12148, 12163 and 12220 for this order's parent chain; the U.S. Code search hit is the 7 U.S.C. 1691 note, not a separate event.
scope_check: The packet inventory has two clauses, section 1 and section 2, covering the whole held text (a short order with no further sections). Section 1 is a continuing direction added to Executive Order 10900; section 2 is a revocation-and-redesignation instruction.
independent_command_check: The only continuing command is the reporting direction in section 1. Section 2 contains no command beyond the one-time amendment of Executive Order 10900. No independent command survives the revocation of Executive Order 10900 under this order; the reissued direction in Executive Order 12220 is a separate command.
savings_check: No savings clause appears in this order. Executive Order 12220 contains no saving provision for Executive Order 10900 or its amendments in its revocation section; the continuing reporting function is carried by Executive Order 12220's own text.

research_rationale: Executive Order 7565 of February 27, 1937 exempts Joseph W. Austin, foreman carpenter in the Capitol Building under the Architect of the Capitol, from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404; 5 U.S.C. 715a) and continues him in the service for a fixed period ending March 1, 1938. The working text is the machine-read government printing in Executive_Orders_7262-8027 (scanned pages 272-273, closing number tag 7565), disclosed as a provisional working text under owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-transcription-as-text.md; original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved. The order's own terms end the exemption on March 1, 1938. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md the end is recorded as the stated date, inclusive; the exclusive reading (the exemption ends when March 1, 1938 begins, so its last day is February 28, 1938) is the alternative a reviewer should see. The four machine searches in the packet (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog dispositions, and the held-text search on the person's name) each report no hit for this order; a name search of the held order texts that I ran separately found only this order and Executive Order 6976 of February 26, 1935, the earlier exemption this order's recital names.
savings_reason: The order grants one named employee a time-limited exemption from automatic separation and contains no savings clause, delegation, reporting duty or other command that could survive March 1, 1938; the bounded searches found no later instrument and no statute or regulation that cites the order.
earlier_end_check: Searched held order texts for the name Joseph W. Austin: only Executive Order 6976 of February 26, 1935 (the earlier exemption, to March 1, 1937) and this order appear, so no later order extends, amends or revokes the exemption. No held source shows Austin's separation, death or retirement before March 1, 1938, so no earlier end is established and the stated date is the first end the held evidence supports. The 1944 WPA numbered list (1937 Feb 27, p. 655) also records the exemption as running until March 1, 1938.
scope_check: The order is one operative paragraph: recitals quoting section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, the finding that the public interest requires continuing Austin, and one ordering sentence. The packet inventory has a single clause, EO:7565#whole, covering characters 213-1401 of the held printing, which spans all of it.
